name: supply-sophie-unanswered-round
narrative: Sophie runs RUTF procurement for the Connect-RUTF program. 17 days ago she asked six suppliers to quote tender 2: half have never answered, despite two reminders, and she forwards whatever does arrive to an AI that records it. Sophie opens tender 2 and reads where it stands: collecting quotes past its deadline, three of six answered and three silent, each supplier's state, the suppliers it waits on with when she last chased each, and that the tender has not settled how import duties are handled. She opens the reminder drafted for Sahel, which says when Sahel was asked and last reminded, and records today's chase from the draft itself. Sahel answers with a quote; Sophie forwards it, and in the tender's history, turned to replies only, Sahel's email comes first: she opens it beside what the AI recorded from it, the reply dated the day it came in. On the comparison, side by side, no quote can be compared yet: the tender's import duty terms are not settled, so Harmattan's carriage-paid quote, which leaves the import to us, waits on them; Kanem has not stated its pack, and Sahel's quote is in euros with no exchange rate recorded. Back on the tender she settles import duty in its Terms box: we import, under the program's duty waiver. Northgate's three questions are still on her, and Reply opens an email drafted with the three questions, an answer to write under each. The comparison then costs the quotes we import under the waiver: Harmattan's becomes comparable, while Kanem's pack and Sahel's freight and exchange rate are still missing. Importing makes the paperwork hers, and tender 1 shows what that means: its order with Harmattan is at customs, held, waiting on us. Its status view shows nothing received yet, the invoice billed above the agreed price and the days it is late, and On us lists the documents owed to the forwarder and the invoice to review; the forwarder's email in the order's history says the trucks are held at the border on our import permit. Back on her overview, every tender and order reads its stage, its next move and whose move it is: tender 2 and the order are hers, and a RUSF tender she asked two days ago waits on its suppliers, with the moves on her counted against those waiting on suppliers.

sophie.intro: Sophie buys RUTF for the Connect-RUTF program; suppliers and the freight forwarder email her, and she forwards what they send to an AI that records it.

scenes.narrative: Sophie asked six suppliers to quote tender 2; only three of the six have replied, though she chased the others twice. She opens the tender and reads where it stands: collecting quotes with its deadline passed, three answered and three silent, each supplier's state, the suppliers it waits on with when she last chased each, and that the tender has not settled how import duties are handled. She wants the record to keep telling her the truth: what the answers left out, and whose move it is.
scenes.title: Half the tender never answered

scenes.narrative: Sophie opens the tender's draft emails at the reminder drafted for Sahel: it says when Sahel was asked and when she last reminded them, and under the message the Chased on field already holds today's date beside Record chase, so the chase she sends is recorded from the draft itself. Back on the tender's Invitations, Sahel's row is marked: last chased today, the third reminder.
scenes.title: She chases Sahel from a drafted reminder

features.description: Between scenes 2 and 3 the AI records Sahel's emailed quote and reply over the labs MCP with source ref, excerpt and sender.

scenes.narrative: Sahel answers the reminder with a quote and Sophie forwards it to the AI. She lands on the tender's history, turned to replies only, where Sahel's email comes first. She opens Sahel's own email and reads who wrote it and that it was forwarded in, with the time it was recorded, the excerpt of what Sahel wrote, and below it what the AI recorded from it, the reply dated the day it came in, so she can check the record against Sahel's words.
scenes.title: Sahel finally answers, and she opens the email

features.description: The comparison sets every quote side by side, one row per fact, and marks each fact a quote has not stated, without ranking quotes that cannot be compared; a quote missing a fact stays out of the count whatever the duty terms.

features.description: A line at the top of the comparison states the tender's import duty terms; while they are not settled, every quote whose Incoterm leaves the import to us waits on them.
features.verify: Playwright: [data-testid=comparison-duty-terms] reads 'Import duty: not settled'; Harmattan Therapeutics' [data-testid=grid-status] reads 'Waiting on our duty terms'

scenes.narrative: Sophie opens the comparison, every quote side by side, and none can be compared yet, for more than one reason. The tender's import duty terms are not settled, and Harmattan quotes carriage paid to Kano, which leaves the import to us, so its duty is ours to cost and its column waits on our terms. Each quote's other gaps are marked where they fall: Kanem has not stated its pack, and Sahel's new quote is in euros, with no exchange rate recorded yet. Settling the terms would free only the quotes that leave the import to us; Kanem's pack and Sahel's rate are still owed.
scenes.title: No quote can be compared yet: duty terms unsettled, facts missing

scenes.narrative: Back on the tender, Sophie settles import duty in its Terms box: we import, under the program's duty waiver, and the box reads the waiver, just recorded. Northgate's three questions are still on her under On us, and Reply opens an email drafted with the three questions, an answer to write under each. She opens the comparison again: the duty line reads the waiver, the Import duty row is settled for the quotes we import, and Harmattan's quote is now comparable, one of three; Kanem's and Sahel's still wait on their missing facts.
scenes.title: She settles the tender's duty terms and replies to Northgate

scenes.narrative: Importing makes the paperwork hers, and tender 1 shows what that means: its order with Harmattan for 2,000 cartons is at customs, held, waiting on us. The status view shows nothing received yet, the invoice billed above the agreed price and how many days late it is, and On us lists the documents owed to the forwarder and the invoice to review. The invoice's lines read billed against agreed, what we owe to clear the shipment lists the import permit and the customs declaration, each to mark provided, and the forwarder's email in the order's history says the trucks are held at the border until the permit is lodged.
scenes.title: Tender 1's order: held on our permit, billed high

scenes.narrative: Back on her overview, Sophie reads the moves counted on her against those waiting on suppliers, then each row: tender 2 still collecting quotes, its next move hers; a RUSF tender for Maiduguri she asked three suppliers about two days ago, still collecting quotes, its next move theirs; and the tender 1 order at customs, its next move hers.
scenes.title: Whose move each procurement is, ours or the suppliers'
